page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-64-lssd is a compute-optimized server instance featuring 64 vCPUs and 248 GB of RAM. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 32 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. Cache specifications include 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The hardware configuration integrates six local NVMe SSDs totaling 2078 GB of local storage, while omitting dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates high-tier processing capabilities. The server achieves top-tier status in Geekbench single-core (2612.0) and multi-core (26866.0) metrics, alongside a Passmark CPU score of 92193.75. Cryptographic and vector instruction sets are supported, including AVX-512 and VAES, which contribute to a Passmark CPU extended instructions score of 118981.01. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only large block bandwidth of 206.38 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 136.56 GB/sec. Database operations perform in the top tier, with Passmark database operations reaching 42358.33 and Redis SET operations registering at 113.85 million operations per second.

The inclusion of 2078 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside a high vCPU count provides high resource density for storage-intensive and compute-heavy workloads. However, the memory-to-vCPU ratio is relatively low at 3.88 GB per core, which represents a tradeoff for memory-bound applications. Qualitatively, the instance offers high compute and storage efficiency for workloads that do not require GPU acceleration. It is suited for software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and medium-scale LLM inference, where it achieves 44.69 tokens per second for text generation on a 7B model.

Powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor with 32 physical cores, this instance delivers top-tier CPU and memory performance without integrated GPU hardware. Benchmarks show strong capabilities, including a Passmark CPU score of 92193.75 and a Passmark database operations score of 42358.33. The system supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and VAES. With 3.88 GB of RAM per core, the instance balances high-density local storage with compute capacity, making it suitable for database management, software compilation, static web serving, and medium-scale language model inference.
